acceptanceCriteria: script/check-line-citations.sh --relocate (or a make target) rewrites citations whose anchored content moved, without changing the hashes, and lists the ones it cannot place
it hashes in process, not with one subprocess per candidate offset; 21 citations finish in under 5 s
--hash on a path that is conflicted or missing from stage 0 exits non-zero with a message naming the unmerged index entry
line-citations-test covers a shifted range, an ambiguous duplicate match and an unstaged conflicted path
body:
Observed 2026-10-21 while merging nine lanes into batch-1021b, and reported by the hosts-mcp-panel lane. Every merge that moves lines in a cited Go file (internal/contextindex/index.go, cmd/corvint/harness.go, help.go) leaves line citations `path:a-b@hash` whose anchor hash is unchanged but whose line numbers are stale. Lanes rerun line-citations-check several times and repin by hand. The orchestrator wrote a scratch relocate script twice (scan +/-60 lines per citation, calling script/check-line-citations.sh --hash once per offset), which took over 3 minutes for 21 citations. It also falsely reported every citation unmatched while the cited file was unstaged in a conflicted merge, because --hash reads the git index (stage 0) and fails on a conflicted path without saying so.
Expected: one command repins every citation whose hash appears at another position in the cited file, in process, and leaves genuinely changed ones for review.
